items.title_orig: Eddie Vedder’s ‘Better Believe’ Video Goes Behind The Scenes
items.article_text:
Written by SPIN Staff | 
  
  
    August 21, 2026 - 10:45 am

Eddie Vedder’s “Better Believe” now has a visual record of the collaboration that brought the song to life, with a new behind-the-scenes video documenting the Pearl Jam frontman’s work with the Obama Foundation and Chicago youth arts nonprofit Guitars Over Guns,  which uses music, mentorship and the arts to create opportunities for young people.

As previously reported, the song came together for the dedication of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago on June 18, where Vedder performed it alongside artists and students connected to Guitars Over Guns. “When you pour into a community and you give resources to people who need them, it makes the whole world a better place,” says 21-year-old rapper Myskie. “It takes nothing to help and to just be useful to a community. It changes people’s lives. It changes the world.”

The new video traces that process from the studio to the stage, highlighting sessions at Columbia College Chicago where Audio Arts students and alumni worked alongside young Guitars Over Guns musicians. The collaboration was facilitated by Andre “Add-2” Daniels, a Columbia adjunct professor and Guitars Over Guns’ Chicago regional director.

The song was co-written by Vedder, Giselle Castro, Daniels, Jeremiah Fristoe, Mason Harris, Michael “Myskie” Hightower, Naomi Owens, Joy Viltz and Iya Waters, with production from Andrew Watt, Daniels, Paul LaMalfa and Vedder. All royalties earned by Vedder and the song’s co-writers will benefit Guitars Over Guns.

“What an honor for all of us to be here on this day,” Vedder told the audience at the Obama Presidential Center dedication. “President Obama was aware that I would be playing music with young musicians from the neighborhood. But when he heard we were writing an original piece, a song just for the occasion, he said, ‘That might be a lot of work.’ And as usual, he was right. But it’s been great work and it’s everything the center stands for — its inclusivity, its access to resources, its mentorship and opportunity. So, we thank you for this opportunity.”
